named_events.loss_description: significantly impacted business activity, led to decreased business activity in many segments, decreased fleet sizes or laid-up vehicles, declined new car sales, reduced road and vehicle usage, dramatically fell claims frequencies during lockdowns, increased used car prices driving inflation in cost of replacing written-off vehicles.

limited impact on ERS' ability to trade because its business is focused on UK motor insurance, but remains a risk to the supply chain for car manufacturers and car parts suppliers, which may further exacerbate claims inflation.

transfer of legacy EEA business and insurance liabilities to LIC, and purchase of 100% quota share reinsurance policy by LIC to cover these liabilities. The combined effect of the two transactions had no economic impact for the Syndicate.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 218 experienced a gross prior year reserve release of GBP 15.2 million in 2020, primarily driven by favourable claims development in recent years. The managing agent noted that favourable reserves movements meant there was not sufficiently adverse aggregate experience to trigger a recovery, and the syndicate continued to benefit from guaranteed interest payments. The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted business activity, leading to reduced road usage and dramatically lower claims frequencies during lockdowns, which offset higher claims costs due to increased used car prices. Brexit was noted as a risk to the supply chain and potential claims inflation, while a Part VII transfer had no economic impact.

The impact of COVID-19 on frequencies and severities, with lockdown measures reducing road usage. Severities could be impacted from suppliers delays and late reported claims from third parties.

Brexit: There remains a risk to the supply chain for car manufacturers and car parts suppliers, which may further exacerbate the claims inflation. External factors could continue to increase claim severities, such as the depreciation of the pound affecting the prices of imported parts.
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development is calculated from the gross claims development triangle, excluding the '2010 & prior' aggregate column and the two most recent underwriting years (2019 and 2020) as per instructions. Note 7 'Movement in prior accident year's provision for claims outstanding' provides a net release of GBP 18.163m, which is not used for the gross PYD figure.
